evidence.quote: Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.reasoning: Mission (GBR coral monitoring via fluid lensing), rationale, single-spacecraft justification and users/operator/funding all addressed with literature references. Detail is good though some claims lack depth.

evidence.quote: an altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924°
Systems Tool Kit 11 (STK) was used to calculate access periods
A span of five years is a sound estimate

criteria.reasoning: All major requirements addressed: Vega E from Kourou, SSO elements table, manoeuvres, Mt Pleasant station, STK access report, 5-year duration, drag-sail EOL. Errors: contradictory altitude/resolution statement, garbled EOL text, no hand calculations shown, STK files not evidenced.

evidence.quote: A specific launch vehicle – the Vega E – has been selected although it has not been built yet.

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions summarise each segment and note risks (Vega E availability), but remain largely a recap without quantitative outcomes or recommendations.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

criteria.reasoning: Clear structure and headings; executive summary present. But figures lack numbered captions, bibliography is bare URLs including Wikipedia (unacceptable per task), and some sentences are garbled/contradictory.

technical_issues.issue: Contradictory statement: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' – low resolution is not desirable.
Contradictory/garbled: satellite 'without thrusters' yet discusses uncontrolled retro-burn descent; drag-sail sentence is incomplete ('to ‘ and is suitable').
Wikipedia used as a source, explicitly disallowed; references are bare URLs without titles/authors/dates.
Justification relies on a Feb-2021 calendar extrapolated to 2025; Vega E selection is speculative and alternatives only briefly noted.

overall: A well-structured, mostly complete mission design for GBR reef monitoring with STK evidence and all major requirements addressed. Weakened by internal contradictions, incomplete EOL discussion, unnumbered figures, and non-compliant referencing (Wikipedia, bare URLs).
